description: CosmoCoders turns real NASA data and space science into an interactive, playable mission design game.
summary:
Moonshot Mission is an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar mission simulator built with Three.js and WebGL that puts players in command of an authentic Moon landing expedition. Users engineer their astronaut loadout under realistic 60 kg mass constraints—balancing life-support oxygen, radiation shielding, and surface mobility—before piloting through atmospheric launch, an interactive 3D cockpit, and deep-space solar storm events. Upon reaching lunar orbit, players evaluate scientifically distinct landing sites, weighing continuous solar power on equatorial ridges against high-value volatile water ice deposits in south pole permanently shadowed craters. Players execute powered descent hazard avoidance and conduct an extravehicular surface walk featuring realistic lunar lighting, regolith dynamics, Earthshine, and life-support telemetry.

By translating complex aerospace principles into engaging, hands-on decision-making, the project addresses the challenge of making deep-space exploration accessible and intuitive. As humanity enters the Artemis era, Moonshot Mission inspires the next generation of STEM innovators by demonstrating the real scientific, technical, and human trade-offs required to explore and sustain life beyond Earth.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

Moonshot Mission is a zero-installation, interactive 3D lunar mission simulator accessible in any modern web browser. It models the end-to-end journey of a human lunar expedition across six interconnected phases, where every engineering decision carries real operational consequences:

  1. Pre-Flight Loadout Engineering: Users design an astronaut’s extravehicular activity (EVA) suit within a strict 60 kg payload budget. Players make tactical trade-offs across suits, helmets, gloves, boots, and life-support packs—balancing mass, radiation shielding ratings, oxygen capacity, and joint mobility.
  2. Launch & Microgravity Cockpit: Following an atmospheric launch sequence, players enter an interactive 3D spacecraft cockpit equipped with active telemetry dashboards, flight computers, navigation instruments, and floating microgravity cabin items.
  3. Translunar Cruise & Solar Storm Survival: While traversing deep space, players encounter extreme space weather—a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME). Drawing on historical solar particle events (such as the massive August 1972 flare), players execute emergency defensive protocols (e.g., repositioning spacecraft equipment/propellant reserves as an improvised shelter), directly impacting the crew’s radiation dosage and vital signs.
  4. Lunar Orbit & Landing Site Science: Upon Translunar Injection and orbital insertion, players survey the lunar surface to evaluate two scientifically authentic target locations:
    • Sunny Ridge (Equatorial Highland Ridge): Near-continuous solar illumination (85%), gentle 3° slopes, direct line-of-sight radio contact with Earth, but low volatile/water-ice reserves.
    • Dark Crater (South Pole Permanently Shadowed Region - PSR): High-risk 14° rim slopes, extreme darkness requiring lander floodlights, and orbital relay comms, but housing rich deposits of trapped water ice essential for sustained exploration.
  5. Powered Descent & Hazard Avoidance: Players manage final braking without atmospheric drag in 1/6th gravity, identifying boulder hazards at low altitude and deciding whether fuel margins permit diverting to a safer touchdown zone.
  6. Lunar Surface EVA Exploration: Stepping off the ladder onto the lunar regolith, users experience a physically modeled environment with procedural terrain, dynamic solar angles, harsh shadows, and subtle Earthshine. Astronauts leave persistent footprints, manage real-time oxygen/power depletion, view Earth suspended 384,400 km away, capture survey photographs, and initiate base camp operations.
